Restricted funds are earmarked for construction and interest, so this understates net funding need. 6. Leases: 17,316 + 49,167 = 66,483 at June 30, 2026; 15,751 + 47,333 = 63,084 at December 31, 2025. Gross notes plus leases: 1,082,552 + 66,483 = 1,149,035. 7. Cash used before financing, six months ended June 30, 2026: operating outflow 30,235 + additions to mineral property, plant and equipment 203,600 + construction prepayments and deposits 9,144 = 242,979. Three months ended June 30, 2026: 15,057 + 131,352 + 4,324 = 150,733. These are analyst sums, not reported free cash flow; they exclude the 254,352 buy-down and treat the sums as outflows. 9. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit story is a single-asset, pre-revenue construction financing. Skeena states that it is "a mining company in the development stage focusing on the construction and development of the Eskay Creek project" (Q2 FS, page:4), and management says the project is "fully permitted and under construction" with "initial production and cash flow in the second quarter of 2027" (Aug 2026 release, page:1). Those timing and quality statements are management language, not audited facts. The financing was rebuilt in the first half of 2026. The June 2024 package with Orion (private placements, a Gold Stream and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan) was replaced on April 10, 2026 by an offering of US$750,000,000 Senior Secured Notes at 8.50% due April 1, 2031. Part of the proceeds repurchased 66.67% of the Gold Stream for US$184,000,000, part went to an interest reserve account covering three semi-annual interest payments, part to a construction disbursement account, and the remainder to general expenses and issuance costs. Creditors therefore sit alongside a reduced stream, new and existing NSR royalties, a growing closure obligation and unreleased restricted cash. The mechanics that matter are release conditions on the restricted accounts, completion-test timing for the Gold Stream percentage, and cost to complete, none of which can be tested from the retained documents. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder is identified. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and transparent in its disclosure of financing events; no creditor-adverse action is documented. The notes' indenture, the Gold Stream and royalty agreements, the annual information form and the technical report are not in the pack, so legal capacity, security and guarantor structure are Insufficient Information. This view is a statement of business and transaction facts and their credit mechanics, not a view on credit quality or recovery.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The principal new debt issue is the offering of US$750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Senior Secured Notes, completed on April 10, 2026 and stated in the statements as 1,036,761 (CAD thousands) (Q2 FS page:12). The notes bear interest at 8.50% per annum payable semi-annually, mature on April 1, 2031, are non-callable for the first two years, and are described as senior secured obligations ranking pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations and senior to all present and future subordinated indebtedness. Before April 1, 2028 the company may redeem some or all of the notes at 100% plus the greater of 1% and a make-whole premium of 50 basis points over the treasury yield, up to 10% at 103%, or up to 40% with net cash proceeds of equity offerings at 108.5%; from April 1, 2028 the redemption price is 104.25% until March 31, 2029, 102.125% until March 31, 2030 and 100% thereafter. A change of control triggers an offer at 101%, and excess proceeds from asset sales above a threshold must be used to offer to purchase the notes (Q2 FS page:12, page:13). Parties other than the issuer (initial purchasers, trustee, any guarantors and the security package) are Not supplied. The use of proceeds as stated in the statements was 254,352 (US$184,000,000) to repurchase 66.67% of the Gold Stream, 130,228 (US$94,208,000) to an interest reserve account representing three semi-annual interest payments, 552,940 (US$400,000,000) to support construction through a disbursement account, and 99,241 (US$71,792,000) for general and administrative expenses and issuance costs. By June 30, 2026, 199,176 (US$145,000,000) of the restricted proceeds had been released and restricted cash stood at 500,853, with cash and cash equivalents of 134,808 (CAD thousands). The company says the proceeds are expected to be sufficient to fund capital requirements through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only "As long as the Company meets the conditions precedent to the Senior Secured Notes", and that additional financing would be needed if funds cannot be released or are insufficient (Q2 FS page:4). The conditions precedent and release mechanics are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The notes replaced the earlier funding plan. Under the June 24, 2024 agreements with Orion, the Project Financing Package consisted of private placements, a Gold Stream with a US$200,000,000 deposit and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan facility (Q3 2025 FS page:4; Q1 FS page:9, page:10). The deposit was fully received by December 31, 2025 and no draws were made on the term loan, which was terminated on April 10, 2026 (Q2 FS page:14). On March 31, 2026 the company entered into an amending agreement to exercise the buy-down option for US$184,000,000 and cancel the option to draw an additional deposit (Q1 FS page:11). The buy-down reduced the Stream Percentage by 66.67%, from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold. The earlier agreement priced the buy-down as the proportional deposit plus an imputed 18% internal rate of return and available for 12 months after the project completion date (Q3 2025 FS page:11); the 2026 early exercise was negotiated, and its pricing basis is not supplied. In the same half-year the company completed an agreement granting third parties a 1% NSR royalty on Eskay Creek and a right to elect an additional NSR royalty or shares, valued at 116,474 and 266,950 at initial recognition respectively (CAD thousands), with a 25,000 prepayment of royalty obligations in the second quarter (Q2 FS page:15, page:16). The equity component of the option, 108,575, was booked to reserves (Q2 FS page:2). Equity funding included a bought deal closed on February 26, 2025 for gross proceeds of 88,347 and another closed on October 8, 2025 for gross proceeds of 143,796 (CAD thousands) (Q3 2025 FS page:12, page:13).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Skeena is a pre-revenue, single-asset construction credit that is funded for now but unproven, and the evidence supports a cautious, not an adverse, view. The strongest support is liquidity: CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash at June 30, 2026, a US$750,000,000 fixed-rate note due April 1, 2031 and an interest reserve covering three semi-annual payments. The weakest point is that no earnings or cost-to-complete figure exists, so leverage, cover and funding adequacy cannot be measured. The outcome turns on delivery of Eskay Creek and the September 30, 2027 completion test, on release of restricted cash, and on the notes' legal terms, which are not in the pack.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The April 10, 2026 notes offering is the pivot of the credit. It replaced the terminated US$350,000,000 term loan, funded the Gold Stream buy-down of US$184,000,000 and placed an interest reserve and a construction disbursement account in restricted cash. The notes carry 8.50% interest, mature on April 1, 2031 and are carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand net of an embedded derivative asset, or CAD 1,082,552 thousand gross; their trading value implies a fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand, which exceeds both figures [CP-1, debt and financing instruments]. The company says proceeds should fund capital needs through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only if the conditions precedent are met; that is management language and the conditions are not supplied [CP-1A, transaction summary; Management Language].

The Gold Stream is a derivative liability of CAD 209,286 thousand and ranks pari passu with the notes; the two royalty liabilities are CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand; lease liabilities are CAD 66,483 thousand; and the closure and reclamation provision rose to CAD 104,777 thousand from CAD 46,227 thousand at December 31, 2025 [CP-1, claims outside the debt figure]. Total liabilities of CAD 1,746,295 thousand exceed shareholders' equity of CAD 170,801 thousand. A surety bond provides reclamation security, with collateral of unstated amount; this corrects the earlier financial base statement that none was found [CP-1A, correction].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is concentrated in one project. Management says Eskay Creek is fully permitted and expects commercial production in 2027, but those are management statements and the retained filings still list permit challenges as a risk [CP-1A, company and operating model; Management Language]. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and supportive of funding, with bought deals in February 2025 and October 2025, and no creditor-adverse action is documented; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Skeena has pre-funded its build: restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand, held for construction and interest, sits beside unrestricted cash of CAD 134,808 thousand, and both together of CAD 635,661 thousand exceed the CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted obligations due within one year [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation, because release of restricted funds is conditional]. The debt is a single fixed-rate bullet maturing on April 1, 2031 with no maturity inside the construction window other than interest, and the interest reserve covers three semi-annual payments [CP-1, debt and financing instruments; Documentary Fact]. The buy-down cut the Gold Stream from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold, reducing the stream's claim on future output [CP-1A, Gold Stream; Documentary Fact]. Equity markets were open to the company in 2025 and the company has documented no debt-funded distributions [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour; Documentary Fact]. The notes' trading value exceeds their carrying amount, which is consistent with, but does not prove, market acceptance of the credit [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Skeena has no revenue, no EBITDA and no operating cash flow: six-month operating cash outflow was CAD 30,235 thousand and additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were CAD 203,600 thousand, so the build depends on financing already raised [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Cost to complete, project budget and schedule are not supplied, so adequacy of the CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash cannot be tested [CP-1A; Insufficient Information]. Claims beside the notes are large relative to the equity base: the Gold Stream, two royalty liabilities, leases and the closure provision, plus a new 1% royalty and an option that could issue shares [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. The company holds US dollar debt and restricted cash while reporting in Canadian dollars, recorded a foreign exchange loss of CAD 17,684 thousand in the six months and does not hedge [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Single-asset concentration means a permit, construction or metallurgical event affects the whole credit [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. If the Gold Stream completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage steps up from 3.52% [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Whether the Gold Stream covenants (debt service coverage and a cash minimum) still apply after the buy-down is Not supplied [CP-1; Insufficient Information].

### Financial base view

Skeena is a development-stage company with no revenue line in any retained statement, so the financial base is a funding and liquidity base, not an earnings base. At June 30, 2026 the company had completed the April 10, 2026 offering of US$750,000,000 Senior Secured Notes (stated as 1,036,761 CAD thousands at issue), used part of the proceeds to repurchase 66.67% of the Gold Stream, and placed the interest reserve and construction disbursement proceeds in restricted accounts. The consolidated balance sheet at that date shows unrestricted cash of 134,808, restricted cash of 500,853, long-term debt carrying value of 1,055,969 and total liabilities of 1,746,295 against shareholders' equity of 170,801 (CAD thousands). The net loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was 139,677, including a 41,736 fair value loss on the Gold Stream derivative and a 17,684 foreign exchange loss; operating cash outflow was 30,235 and additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were 203,600 for the same six months. Because earnings measures do not exist, the report's leverage and interest cover chart cells are Not supplied, and the funding picture is read from cash, restricted cash, the maturity table and the construction commitments. The limits are material: the statements are unaudited, FY2025 full-year flows and the audited notes are not in the pack, cash interest paid for the half-year is not stated, and neither the legal terms of the notes nor the cost to complete is supplied. Debt figures that involve US dollar balances move with exchange rates, and the company states that it does not use derivatives to reduce exposure to foreign exchange risk (Q2 FS, page:10).

### Debt and financing instruments

- **Senior Secured Notes.** Issuer Skeena Resources Limited; no co-issuer is named in the retained pages. Principal US$750,000,000 ("$1,036,761,000 (US$750,000,000)" at issue), 8.50% per annum payable semi-annually, maturing April 1, 2031, non-callable for the first two years, senior secured and ranking pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations (Q2 FS page:12). Redemption: before April 1, 2028 at 100% plus the greater of 1% and a make-whole premium of 50 basis points over the treasury yield, up to 10% at 103%, and up to 40% with equity proceeds at 108.5%; from April 1, 2028 at 104.25% until March 31, 2029, 102.125% until March 31, 2030 and 100% thereafter; change of control put at 101%; asset sale excess proceeds offer (Q2 FS page:12, page:13). Effective interest rate 8.57% (Q2 FS page:13). Guarantors, collateral package, financial covenants and the release conditions for restricted cash: Not supplied (the indenture is not in the pack, and a search of every source for "guarantor", "covenant", "indenture" and "collateral" found none for the notes).
- **Senior Secured Term Loan facility.** US$350,000,000, no draws, terminated April 10, 2026 (Q2 FS page:14). Not a current source of liquidity.

- **Gold Stream.** Derivative liability at fair value through profit or loss. After the April 10, 2026 buy-down of 66.67% for US$184,000,000 (254,352 CAD thousands), the Stream Percentage is 3.52% of payable gold for the life of the mine, rising if the completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 (Q2 FS page:14). Before the buy-down the percentage was 10.55% (Q1 FS page:10). Counterparty is named Orion in the Q1 FS (page:10). Security and covenants are described in the Q1 FS (page:10, page:11) and are discussed under Covenants below.

- **NSR royalty and Additional NSR Royalty Option.** A 1% NSR royalty subject to a minimum paid value of 100,000 CAD thousands and capped at the first 5,000,000 gold equivalent ounces sold, and an option to elect an additional 1.5% royalty, or common shares (2,900,001), or mixed combinations (Q2 FS page:15). Liability components are at amortized cost (Q2 FS page:16). A prepayment of 25,000 was made in the quarter (Q2 FS page:16).

- **Leases and equipment loans.** Lease liabilities 66,483 in total at June 30, 2026. The company also entered into "various vehicle and equipment leases and loan financing" (Q2 FS page:12); the balance of any equipment loans is not separately stated.
- **Co-issuers, other guarantors and subsidiary-level debt:** Not supplied. The statements are consolidated for a single registrant and name no restricted or unrestricted subsidiary group.

### Liquidity

Unrestricted cash and cash equivalents were 134,808 at June 30, 2026 and no committed undrawn facility is disclosed, because the term loan was terminated. Restricted cash totals 500,853, of which 453,925 is current. Of the proceeds placed in the interest reserve and construction disbursement accounts (683,168, US$494,208 thousand), 199,176 (US$145,000 thousand) had been released by June 30, 2026 (Q2 FS page:12). The company states that its anticipated funding is sufficient to commercial production in 2027 only "As long as the Company meets the conditions precedent to the Senior Secured Notes", and that it will need additional financing if the release of funds is not possible or the proceeds are insufficient (Q2 FS page:4; the Q1 FS wording is similar). The company discloses a going concern dependency on executing its business plan (Q2 FS page:4). The cost to complete construction is Not supplied.
### Covenants

No financial maintenance covenant for the Senior Secured Notes is stated in the retained pages. Gold Stream covenants were described in the Q1 FS: a debt service coverage ratio of no less than 1.25:1 for the six months ended on the last date of each quarter after the completion test and a grace period, and minimum unrestricted cash and cash equivalents of at least 25,000 CAD thousands at all times following the full drawdown or cancellation of the Senior Secured Term Loan commitments and the additional deposit, both until the Security Release Date (Q1 FS page:10, page:11). Both commitments were cancelled by April 10, 2026. The Q2 FS does not repeat these terms after the buy-down, so whether they still apply is Not supplied. If the cash minimum still applied, unrestricted cash would exceed it by 109,808 (Calculation 15). The debt service coverage test cannot be computed because no definition inputs or earnings exist. The debt service coverage ratio, the cash minimum and the notes' covenants use definitions that are not supplied and differ from any metric computed in this module.
### Latest quarter and subsequent events

Quarter ended June 30, 2026 events: completion of the notes offering on April 10, 2026 and use of proceeds (Q2 FS page:12); exercise of the Gold Stream buy-down option (Q2 FS page:14); termination of the term loan (Q2 FS page:14); grant of the NSR Royalty and Additional NSR Royalty Option with 266,950 of initial recognition for the option (Q2 FS page:16); royalty prepayment of 25,000 (Q2 FS page:3); closure provision increase to 104,777 with an estimate change of 58,120 in the six months (Q2 FS page:16). The Q2 FS has no subsequent events note. No event between June 30, 2026 and the cutoff is supplied; the pack contains no filing after August 13, 2026 and no Q3 2026 results.
### Definition review
- The issuer reports no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow. No definition is supplied. This module does not invent one.

- "Total debt" here means the Senior Secured Notes only at gross amortized cost (1,082,552) or net carrying value (1,055,969); leases are shown separately. The embedded derivative asset of 26,583 is netted on the balance sheet but is not a cash resource.
- Restricted cash is excluded from "cash" in the liquidity table. It is shown separately because release depends on conditions not supplied.

- The first six months' interest expense is partly capitalized: interest expense on long-term debt, lease and other liabilities, net of interest income on proceeds, was capitalized at 5,402 to mineral property and 13,328 to construction-in-progress (Q2 FS page:11). Gross interest incurred is therefore larger than the 19,851 expensed, and cash interest cannot be derived.
## Calculations
All amounts CAD thousands unless stated. Inputs are the reported figures cited above.
1. Restricted cash: 453,925 + 46,928 = 500,853. Agrees to the financial instruments table (Q2 FS page:7).
2. Total cash including restricted: 134,808 + 500,853 = 635,661.
3. Debt carrying value: 89,352 + 966,617 = 1,055,969. Also 1,082,552 - 26,583 = 1,055,969. Both agree to the printed carrying value.
4. Gross debt less unrestricted cash: 1,082,552 - 134,808 = 947,744. This is a net debt figure on a gross-notes basis, not a ratio, because no EBITDA exists.
5. Gross debt less all cash including restricted: 1,082,552 - 635,661 = 446,891. Restricted funds are earmarked for construction and interest, so this understates net funding need.
7. Working capital: 612,167 - 194,097 = 418,070 including restricted current cash. Excluding current restricted cash: 612,167 - 453,925 = 158,242; 158,242 - 194,097 = -35,855.

8. Cash used before financing, six months ended June 30, 2026: operating outflow 30,235 + additions to mineral property, plant and equipment 203,600 + construction prepayments and deposits 9,144 = 242,979. Three months ended June 30, 2026: 15,057 + 131,352 + 4,324 = 150,733. These are analyst sums, not reported free cash flow; they exclude the 254,352 buy-down and treat the sums as outflows.

9. Cross-checks of the six-month figures against the first quarter (Q1 FS page:1 to page:3): net loss 139,677 - 104,457 = 35,220 (agrees to the three-month loss); additions 203,600 - 72,248 = 131,352 (agrees); operating outflow 30,235 - 15,178 = 15,057 (agrees).
10. Gold Stream derivative roll-forward: 421,902 - 254,352 + 41,736 = 209,286. Agrees to the printed balance (Q2 FS page:15).

11. Notes proceeds allocation: 254,352 + 130,228 + 552,940 + 99,241 = 1,036,761, agrees to the principal. Restricted deposits: 130,228 + 552,940 = 683,168, agrees to the printed total. Cash proceeds: 99,241 + 254,352 = 353,593, agrees to the printed proceeds (Q2 FS page:12).

12. Restricted cash roll: 683,168 - 199,176 = 483,992 against reported restricted cash of 500,853, a difference of 16,861. In US dollar thousands: 494,208 - 145,000 = 349,208 against 352,442 reported (Q2 FS page:10), a difference of 3,234. The sources do not explain either difference; it is not attributed to interest income or exchange.

14. Coupon sizing from printed terms: US$750,000,000 x 8.50% = US$63,750,000 a year, US$31,875,000 per semi-annual payment. Three payments are US$95,625,000, compared with the interest reserve deposit of US$94,208,000, a shortfall of US$1,417,000 against three full coupons that the sources do not explain. At the issue-date ratio of 1,036,761 / 750,000 = 1.382348 CAD per US$, the annual coupon is 63,750 x 1.382348 = 88,125 (rounded). The undiscounted within-one-year long-term debt figure is 88,581 (Q2 FS page:11); the two bases differ and are not reconciled.
15. Gold Stream cash minimum, if it still applied: 134,808 - 25,000 = 109,808 of excess over the minimum.
18. Leverage and interest cover: Not calculable. No EBITDA or revenue is reported, and cash interest paid for the half-year is not stated.

## Next module

Pass to the business and transaction context module (CP-1A) with these limits: reported figures are CAD thousands, unaudited, and for the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026 unless labelled otherwise; the notes' legal terms and the Gold Stream covenant status are Not supplied; and restricted cash of 500,853 is not freely available. That module should describe the Eskay Creek financing structure (notes, Gold Stream buy-down, royalties) using the notes' own wording and carry the missing project budget as a gap. ### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Skeena is a pre-revenue builder of the Eskay Creek gold-silver mine; management expects commercial production in 2027. An April 2026 note issue replaced the term loan and bought back part of the Gold Stream. | Medium | Business and ownership facts rest on statement notes and press-release text; no annual information form, technical report, offtake or financing agreements are supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Eskay Creek is the only development asset described, there is no revenue, and management expects commercial production in 2027. | Debt service before production depends on funds already raised, so construction delivery and timing drive repayment capacity. | Medium |

| The April 10, 2026 notes offering replaced the terminated term loan and funded the Gold Stream buy-down of US$184,000,000. | Funding moved from a drawn facility to a bond with restricted accounts; the Gold Stream remains a pari passu claim at a lower percentage. | High |

| A 1% NSR royalty and an Additional NSR Royalty Option were granted in the first half of 2026, on top of earlier royalties of 4% to 5.5%. | Royalties and the stream take a share of future project output before it reaches debt holders; the option could also add shares. | Medium |

| Equity was raised in bought deals in February 2025 and October 2025; no controlling holder, sponsor or distribution is documented. | Documented behaviour is supportive of funding, but ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed. | Medium |

| Earlier statements show collateral paid to a surety bond provider for reclamation security, which corrects the earlier financial base handoff. | The amount of collateral is not stated, so reclamation security cannot be sized separately from the closure provision of 104,777 (CAD thousands). | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The credit story is a single-asset, pre-revenue construction financing. Skeena states that it is "a mining company in the development stage focusing on the construction and development of the Eskay Creek project" (Q2 FS, page:4), and management says the project is "fully permitted and under construction" with "initial production and cash flow in the second quarter of 2027" (Aug 2026 release, page:1). Those timing and quality statements are management language, not audited facts. The financing was rebuilt in the first half of 2026. The June 2024 package with Orion (private placements, a Gold Stream and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan) was replaced on April 10, 2026 by an offering of US$750,000,000 Senior Secured Notes at 8.50% due April 1, 2031. Part of the proceeds repurchased 66.67% of the Gold Stream for US$184,000,000, part went to an interest reserve account covering three semi-annual interest payments, part to a construction disbursement account, and the remainder to general expenses and issuance costs. Creditors therefore sit alongside a reduced stream, new and existing NSR royalties, a growing closure obligation and unreleased restricted cash. The mechanics that matter are release conditions on the restricted accounts, completion-test timing for the Gold Stream percentage, and cost to complete, none of which can be tested from the retained documents. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder is identified. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and transparent in its disclosure of financing events; no creditor-adverse action is documented. The notes' indenture, the Gold Stream and royalty agreements, the annual information form and the technical report are not in the pack, so legal capacity, security and guarantor structure are Insufficient Information. This view is a statement of business and transaction facts and their credit mechanics, not a view on credit quality or recovery.

Permits and legal challenges are listed as risks (Mar 2026 release page:3). |

After production, a share of payable gold is committed to the Gold Stream: 3.52% of payable gold after the buy-down, against a cash payment of 10% of the gold market price | Documentary Fact | Q2 FS page:1, page:2, page:14 | Revenue durability cannot be assessed before production; see the stream and royalty rows. |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

A change of control triggers an offer at 101%, and excess proceeds from asset sales above a threshold must be used to offer to purchase the notes (Q2 FS page:12, page:13). Parties other than the issuer (initial purchasers, trustee, any guarantors and the security package) are Not supplied. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Skeena is a pre-revenue, single-asset construction credit that is funded for now but unproven. The evidence supports a cautious, not adverse, view; earnings-based leverage and cover cannot be measured. | Medium | No EBITDA, cost to complete, or legal terms for the notes are supplied, and the statements are unaudited interim. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| At June 30, 2026 the company held unrestricted cash of 134,808 and restricted cash of 500,853 (CAD thousands), against 316,513 of undiscounted obligations due within one year. | Near-term obligations are covered only if restricted funds are released as intended; unrestricted cash alone is smaller than that obligation figure. | Medium |

| The Senior Secured Notes of US$750,000,000 at 8.50% mature on April 1, 2031 and are non-callable for the first two years. | No principal falls due during the build, so near-term pressure is interest and construction cost, not refinancing. | High |
| No revenue or EBITDA exists, so leverage and interest cover are not calculable. | The view rests on funding and project delivery, not earnings capacity, so confidence stays limited. | High |

| Claims ahead of or beside the notes include the Gold Stream (209,286), royalties (78,709 and 136,009) and a closure provision of 104,777. | These reduce project cash available to the notes once production starts and raise exposure if the schedule slips. | Medium |

| Execution risk is unquantified: no cost to complete, covenant status after the buy-down, or release conditions are supplied. | Cost overruns or delay would draw on restricted cash and the interest reserve, and could trigger a higher stream percentage. | Medium |
### Credit view

Skeena is a pre-revenue, single-asset construction credit that is funded for now but unproven, and the evidence supports a cautious, not an adverse, view. The strongest support is liquidity: CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash at June 30, 2026, a US$750,000,000 fixed-rate note due April 1, 2031 and an interest reserve covering three semi-annual payments. The weakest point is that no earnings or cost-to-complete figure exists, so leverage, cover and funding adequacy cannot be measured. The outcome turns on delivery of Eskay Creek and the September 30, 2027 completion test, on release of restricted cash, and on the notes' legal terms, which are not in the pack.
### Key findings

Skeena has no revenue and reports no EBITDA, so every earnings-based measure is Not supplied and the credit view rests on funding and project delivery [CP-1, financial base; Not calculable]. At June 30, 2026 the company held CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash, with CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted financial liabilities and commitments due within one year; the restricted balance is what makes the near-term picture covered, and its release conditions are not supplied [CP-1, liquidity and maturity table; CP-1A, transaction summary].

The April 10, 2026 notes offering is the pivot of the credit. It replaced the terminated US$350,000,000 term loan, funded the Gold Stream buy-down of US$184,000,000 and placed an interest reserve and a construction disbursement account in restricted cash. The notes carry 8.50% interest, mature on April 1, 2031 and are carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand net of an embedded derivative asset, or CAD 1,082,552 thousand gross; their trading value implies a fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand, which exceeds both figures [CP-1, debt and financing instruments]. The company says proceeds should fund capital needs through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only if the conditions precedent are met; that is management language and the conditions are not supplied [CP-1A, transaction summary; Management Language].

Other claims sit beside the notes. The Gold Stream is a derivative liability of CAD 209,286 thousand and ranks pari passu with the notes; the two royalty liabilities are CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand; lease liabilities are CAD 66,483 thousand; and the closure and reclamation provision rose to CAD 104,777 thousand from CAD 46,227 thousand at December 31, 2025 [CP-1, claims outside the debt figure]. Total liabilities of CAD 1,746,295 thousand exceed shareholders' equity of CAD 170,801 thousand. A surety bond provides reclamation security, with collateral of unstated amount; this corrects the earlier financial base statement that none was found [CP-1A, correction].

The business is concentrated in one project. Management says Eskay Creek is fully permitted and expects commercial production in 2027, but those are management statements and the retained filings still list permit challenges as a risk [CP-1A, company and operating model; Management Language]. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and supportive of funding, with bought deals in February 2025 and October 2025, and no creditor-adverse action is documented; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Skeena has pre-funded its build: restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand, held for construction and interest, sits beside unrestricted cash of CAD 134,808 thousand, and both together of CAD 635,661 thousand exceed the CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted obligations due within one year [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation, because release of restricted funds is conditional]. The debt is a single fixed-rate bullet maturing on April 1, 2031 with no maturity inside the construction window other than interest, and the interest reserve covers three semi-annual payments [CP-1, debt and financing instruments; Documentary Fact]. The buy-down cut the Gold Stream from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold, reducing the stream's claim on future output [CP-1A, Gold Stream; Documentary Fact]. Equity markets were open to the company in 2025 and the company has documented no debt-funded distributions [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour; Documentary Fact]. The notes' trading value exceeds their carrying amount, which is consistent with, but does not prove, market acceptance of the credit [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Skeena has no revenue, no EBITDA and no operating cash flow: six-month operating cash outflow was CAD 30,235 thousand and additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were CAD 203,600 thousand, so the build depends on financing already raised [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Cost to complete, project budget and schedule are not supplied, so adequacy of the CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash cannot be tested [CP-1A; Insufficient Information]. Claims beside the notes are large relative to the equity base: the Gold Stream, two royalty liabilities, leases and the closure provision, plus a new 1% royalty and an option that could issue shares [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. The company holds US dollar debt and restricted cash while reporting in Canadian dollars, recorded a foreign exchange loss of CAD 17,684 thousand in the six months and does not hedge [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Single-asset concentration means a permit, construction or metallurgical event affects the whole credit [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. If the Gold Stream completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage steps up from 3.52% [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Whether the Gold Stream covenants (debt service coverage and a cash minimum) still apply after the buy-down is Not supplied [CP-1; Insufficient Information].

| Assessment | Funded but unproven single-asset construction credit; cautious, not adverse; funding adequacy to commercial production is not measurable | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 liquidity, debt and maturity figures; CP-1A business and transaction rows | Medium |

| Thesis | Skeena's creditors are protected for now by pre-funded, partly restricted cash and a long-dated fixed-rate bond, while repayment ultimately depends on delivering Eskay Creek on schedule and on documents the pack does not contain | Analyst Interpretation | As above | Medium |
| Leverage and interest cover | Not calculable: no EBITDA or revenue; cash interest for the half-year not stated | Insufficient Information | CP-1 chart data | Not assessable |

| Management timing and quality claims | Commercial production in 2027; fully permitted; lowest-cost claims are management language and are not adopted | Management Language | CP-1A company and operating model | Not assessable |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Construction cost or schedule overrun | Spend of CAD 203,600 thousand in six months, commitments of CAD 168,356 thousand and payables-funded additions of CAD 75,178 thousand draw on restricted cash; cost to complete is not supplied | Overrun would consume the construction account and interest reserve, and could require new financing, which the company itself says would be needed | Material |

| Restricted cash release | CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash depends on release conditions not supplied; CAD 199,176 thousand had been released by June 30, 2026 | If release stalls, unrestricted cash of CAD 134,808 thousand is the only free liquidity against CAD 316,513 thousand of obligations due within one year | Material |

| Gold Stream completion test | The stream percentage steps up from 3.52% if the completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 | Delay raises the claim on gold output at the same time as funding is stretched | Material |

| Documentation opacity | Indenture, guarantors, security, covenants and the stream agreement are not supplied | Priority, enforcement rights and covenant headroom cannot be assessed; this is a limitation, not an adverse finding | Material |
